system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Brussels, Belgium. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Brussels itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Brussels space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Ixelles/Louise, Sablon/Centre, Saint-Gilles/Forest, Dansaert/Canal, Molenbeek/Anderlecht, Uccle) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Brussels spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Brussels, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Xavier Hufkens
galleries.note: Belgium's leading international gallery since 1987; Louise Bourgeois, Sterling Ruby, Nicolas Party, Tracey Emin; two Ixelles spaces and constant fair presence.

galleries.name: WIELS
galleries.note: Non-collecting contemporary art centre in the former Wielemans brewery; the city's most influential exhibition and residency programme, a magnet for artists moving to Brussels.

galleries.name: Almine Rech
galleries.note: Brussels outpost of the global Paris-founded gallery; blue-chip and market-leading younger painters, strong fair programme.

galleries.name: Gladstone Gallery
galleries.note: New York mega-gallery's only European space, open since 2008; museum-calibre shows of Ugo Rondinone, Anicka Yi, Carrie Mae Weems and the estate of Keith Haring.

galleries.name: Galerie Greta Meert
galleries.note: Founded 1988 in a Bruno Vanden Broecke-restored building; rigorous minimal and conceptual line (Gerhard Richter, On Kawara, Marthe Wéry, Ann Veronica Janssens).

galleries.name: Jan Mot
galleries.note: Conceptual bellwether since 1995; Tino Sehgal, Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster, David Lamelas, Manon de Boer — its newspaper invitations are a genre of their own.

galleries.name: Meessen (Meessen De Clercq)
galleries.note: Since 2008 a cerebral, poetic programme (Nicolás Lamas, Claudio Parmiggiani, Ignasi Aballí) with a steady presence at Art Basel and Frieze.

galleries.name: rodolphe janssen
galleries.note: Open since 1991; early champion of Wolfgang Tillmans, Sam Falls, Thomas Lerooy and a generation of Belgian painters; major fair presence.

galleries.name: Dépendance
galleries.note: Michael Callies's sharp, artist-driven gallery; Lucy McKenzie, Michael Krebber, Josef Strau — a key node of the Cologne–Brussels axis.

galleries.name: C L E A R I N G
galleries.note: Brooklyn-founded gallery whose Forest warehouse near WIELS launched Harold Ancart, Calvin Marcus and Sebastian Black to international attention.

galleries.name: Mendes Wood DM
galleries.note: São Paulo gallery's European base in a townhouse near the Sablon; Paulo Nazareth, Sonia Gomes, Lucas Arruda and a strong Global South programme.

galleries.name: Baronian
galleries.note: Albert Baronian has shown Arte Povera, Supports/Surfaces and Belgian contemporaries since 1973 — the dean of the Brussels scene.

galleries.name: Galerie Nathalie Obadia
galleries.note: Paris gallery's Brussels space since 2008; Carole Benzaken, Jorge Queiroz, Fiona Rae, plus strong photography and painting.

galleries.name: Templon
galleries.note: Daniel Templon's Brussels branch in a converted garage; Kehinde Wiley, Chiharu Shiota, Omar Ba and other international names.

galleries.name: Harlan Levey Projects
galleries.note: Research-driven gallery with two Forest spaces; Marcin Dudek, Emmanuel Van der Auwera, TR Ericsson — high institutional traction for a young house.

galleries.name: La Loge
galleries.note: Modernist former masonic temple turned art space; commissions and solo presentations that regularly precede artists' museum breakthroughs.

galleries.name: Établissement d'en face
galleries.note: Artist-run since 1992 and the most respected experimental space in the city; a launchpad for radical, anti-commercial projects.

galleries.name: Michel Rein
galleries.note: Paris gallery's Brussels space; politically engaged programme with Jota Castro, Maria Thereza Alves, Raphaël Zarka.

galleries.name: Maruani Mercier
galleries.note: Large Louise space with an American-leaning roster (Alex Katz, Mickalene Thomas, Sam Gilliam estate work) and satellites in Knokke and Zaventem.

galleries.name: Dvir Gallery
galleries.note: Tel Aviv gallery's European space, bringing Latifa Echakhch, Jonathan Monk and Douglas Gordon to a Brussels audience.

galleries.name: Bozar – Centre for Fine Arts
galleries.note: Horta-designed non-collecting arts centre; its large contemporary surveys and Belgian mid-career retrospectives set national agendas.

galleries.name: Sorry We're Closed
galleries.note: Sébastien Janssen's gallery, born as a street-facing vitrine; irreverent, queer-inflected programme with growing international visibility.

galleries.name: Super Dakota
galleries.note: Young-generation gallery with a sharp eye for emerging American and European painters and sculptors.

galleries.name: Irène Laub Gallery
galleries.note: Formerly Aeroplastics-adjacent Irène Laub Projects; conceptual and process-based artists, consistent fair presence and institutional placements.

galleries.name: Fondation CAB
galleries.note: Hubert Bonnet's foundation in an Art Deco building devoted to minimal and conceptual art, with a residency and satellite spaces abroad.

galleries.name: La Verrière – Fondation d'entreprise Hermès
galleries.note: Corporate-funded but curatorially independent glass-roofed space; long-running curated cycles that punch far above its size.

galleries.name: Argos – Centre for Audiovisual Arts
galleries.note: Europe's key archive and exhibition platform for artists' film and video, with a distribution arm and major screening programme.

galleries.name: La Patinoire Royale – Galerie Valérie Bach
galleries.note: A 3,000 m² 19th-century skating rink hosting ambitious solo shows and historical surveys — the largest private exhibition space in the city.

galleries.name: Levy Delval
galleries.note: Elaine Levy and Xavier Delval's gallery for conceptually rigorous emerging and mid-career artists; a critics' favourite.

galleries.name: Damien & The Love Guru
galleries.note: Small, internationally networked gallery whose emerging roster and fair presentations (Liste, Paris Internationale) draw outsized attention.

galleries.name: La Maison de Rendez-Vous
galleries.note: Shared Brussels venue where international galleries (Bosse & Baum, Sundy and others) rotate exhibitions — a model for post-fair collaboration.

galleries.name: Stems Gallery
galleries.note: Market-savvy young gallery promoting a new generation of figurative painters, with an energetic fair calendar.

galleries.name: CENTRALE for contemporary art
galleries.note: City of Brussels art centre in a former power station; solo shows of Belgian artists plus project boxes for emerging practices.

galleries.name: Island
galleries.note: Curator-run space with a discursive, research-heavy programme that has become a fixture of the city's alternative circuit.

galleries.name: Komplot
galleries.note: Nomadic curatorial collective since 2002; exhibitions, residencies and publications that shaped Brussels' independent scene.

galleries.name: Deborah Bowmann
galleries.note: Artist-run space and fictional persona blurring design, display and exhibition-making; widely cited by younger curators.

galleries.name: Galerie Pierre Marie Giraud
galleries.note: International reference for contemporary ceramics, glass and studio objects; shows Japanese and European masters alongside artists.

galleries.name: Ballon Rouge
galleries.note: Collective-model gallery founded on itinerant projects, now with a permanent Brussels space and a strongly international emerging roster.

galleries.name: Aeroplastics Contemporary
galleries.note: Since 1998 a provocative programme mixing American and Belgian artists; early supporter of Nick Cave and Erwin Wurm in Belgium.

galleries.name: Keitelman Gallery
galleries.note: Historically minded gallery bridging post-war abstraction, photography and contemporary positions.

galleries.name: Hopstreet Gallery
galleries.note: Quiet, drawing- and photography-focused programme with a loyal institutional following.

galleries.name: Galerie La Forest Divonne
galleries.note: Paris–Brussels gallery in a converted industrial space; painting-led programme of French and Belgian artists.

galleries.name: Fondation Boghossian – Villa Empain
galleries.note: Restored Art Deco villa staging thematic East–West exhibitions and residencies for contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Fondation Thalie
galleries.note: Nathalie Guiot's foundation combining exhibitions, residencies and publishing, with an ecological and feminist emphasis.

galleries.name: Fondation A Stichting
galleries.note: Photography foundation near WIELS presenting rigorous historical and contemporary photobook-based exhibitions.

galleries.name: Vanhaerents Art Collection
galleries.note: Private collection in a converted warehouse, opening long-running thematic displays of major international contemporary art to the public.

galleries.name: ISELP
galleries.note: Institute for higher studies in plastic arts; exhibitions, lectures and criticism that anchor the francophone art discourse.

galleries.name: Contretype
galleries.note: Long-standing centre for contemporary photography with residencies and a focus on urban imagery.

galleries.name: Hangar
galleries.note: Photography art centre showing documentary and contemporary photographers, with an ambitious international exhibition rhythm.

galleries.name: Botanique
galleries.note: Cultural centre whose galleries in the former orangery run a consistent contemporary and photographic exhibition programme.

galleries.name: Beursschouwburg
galleries.note: Interdisciplinary arts house whose exhibitions and commissions support younger, often post-colonial and queer practices.

galleries.name: Greylight Projects
galleries.note: Artist-run residency and exhibition platform in a former chapel complex; a hub for experimental and cross-border projects.

galleries.name: Rectangle
galleries.note: Billboard-format commissioning platform putting artists' work into public space; low-budget, high-visibility model.

galleries.name: Zsenne ArtLab
galleries.note: Artist-run laboratory near Anneessens offering short, experimental exhibitions to emerging Brussels-based artists.

galleries.name: MAAC – Maison d'Art Actuel des Chartreux
galleries.note: Non-profit house for current art with exhibitions, residencies and support for young Belgian artists.

galleries.name: SB34
galleries.note: Organisation running temporary art spaces in buildings awaiting redevelopment; residencies and exhibitions across several Brussels sites.

galleries.name: L'Hectolitre
galleries.note: Long-running artist-run space in the Marolles known for scrappy, generous shows by young Brussels artists.

galleries.name: Bureau des Réalités
galleries.note: Small gallery with a conceptual, socially engaged line and a strong presence at emerging-sector fairs.

galleries.name: LMNO
galleries.note: Emerging-focused gallery mixing digital, video and installation practices with an international young roster.

galleries.name: Rossicontemporary
galleries.note: Rivoli Building gallery with an abstraction- and materials-led programme of Belgian and international artists.

galleries.name: Felix Frachon Gallery
galleries.note: Young dealer showing emerging painters and sculptors, active at satellite fairs and in group-show collaborations.

galleries.name: Jozsa Gallery
galleries.note: Intimate space in the Saint-Georges gallery cluster with a mainly emerging European roster.

galleries.name: Ricou Gallery
galleries.note: Sébastien Ricou's gallery, connecting Brussels with Eastern European and conceptual positions.

galleries.name: Galerie Fred Lanzenberg
galleries.note: Veteran Ixelles gallery active since the 1970s, bridging Belgian modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Alice Gallery
galleries.note: Key Brussels address for graphic, street and lowbrow-derived contemporary art with a devoted collector base.

galleries.name: Galerie Pascal Polar
galleries.note: Large Charleroi-road space mixing contemporary art, photography and historical surrealist-linked material.

galleries.name: Galerie Faider
galleries.note: Small Saint-Gilles gallery with a consistent programme of Belgian painters and sculptors.

galleries.name: Galerie Didier Devillez
galleries.note: Specialist in Belgian surrealism, CoBrA legacies and their contemporary heirs; also a publisher.

galleries.name: Galerie Martine Ehmer
galleries.note: Independent gallery supporting mid-career Belgian artists and works on paper.

galleries.name: Galerie Quadri
galleries.note: Long-established gallery devoted to geometric and constructivist abstraction in Belgium.

galleries.name: Le Salon d'Art
galleries.note: Gallery and antiquarian bookshop behind a historic hairdressing salon; contemporary drawing, prints and photography since 1978.

galleries.name: Spazio Nobile
galleries.note: Applied-arts and collectible-design gallery with a curatorial, seasonal exhibition model and international fair presence.

galleries.name: PULS Contemporary Ceramics
galleries.note: Reference gallery for contemporary ceramic art, showing leading European and Japanese makers.

galleries.name: Galerie Patrick Derom
galleries.note: Sablon dealer in Belgian modernism who regularly stages contemporary sculpture and Magritte-related projects.

galleries.name: Elisa Platteau & Cie Galerie
galleries.note: Painting-focused gallery supporting a small group of Belgian and French artists over the long term.

galleries.name: Galerie Zwart Huis
galleries.note: Knokke-founded gallery whose Brussels space shows Belgian post-war figures alongside contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Galerie 100 Titres
galleries.note: Dedicated to art brut and outsider art, a field with deep Brussels roots and growing institutional interest.

galleries.name: Maison Grégoire
galleries.note: Modernist house-museum-turned-venue hosting site-responsive contemporary exhibitions and concerts.

galleries.name: L'Escaut
galleries.note: Architects' cooperative whose canal-side hall stages exhibitions, performances and interdisciplinary projects.

galleries.name: Atelier 34zero Muzeum
galleries.note: Artist-founded museum-workshop with an outdoor sculpture park and residencies on the city's green edge.

galleries.name: Maison des Arts de Schaerbeek
galleries.note: Municipal 19th-century mansion offering free contemporary exhibitions with a strong local artist focus.

galleries.name: Recyclart
galleries.note: Socially rooted arts platform combining exhibitions, workshops and music in a repurposed industrial site.

galleries.name: Q-O2
galleries.note: Workspace for experimental music and sound art, with residencies, installations and public presentations.

galleries.name: Strokar Inn
galleries.note: Large urban-art venue and street-art incubator; commercially oriented but a significant public platform for graffiti-derived practice.

galleries.name: Nardone Contemporary
galleries.note: Small dealer active in Brussels for over two decades with a photography- and multiples-oriented programme.
